content.overview: Section 42 permits a company to make a private placement of securities only to Board-identified persons, subject to the prescribed numerical cap (fifty or such higher number as prescribed, excluding QIBs and ESOP employees under s. 62(1)(b)), prescribed offer form, no renunciation, banking-channel payment, allotment within sixty days (or refund with 12% interest), and return of allotment.
content.glance: Private placement only to identified persons within the numerical cap; no renunciation; allot within 60 days or refund with interest.
content.study: A private placement is any offer or invitation to subscribe or issue of securities to a select group of persons (other than by way of public offer) through a private placement offer-cum-application satisfying section 42. Identified persons are selected by the Board. The number in a financial year must not exceed fifty or the prescribed higher number, excluding QIBs and employees under an ESOP scheme under section 62(1)(b). The offer and application must be in the prescribed form to recorded identified persons and must not carry a right of renunciation. Subscription money must be paid through banking channels, not cash. Securities must be allotted within sixty days of receipt of application money, failing which the money must be repaid within fifteen days of the expiry of sixty days, with interest at twelve per cent per annum from the expiry of the sixtieth day if not so repaid. Application money must be kept in a separate bank account. A return of allotment must be filed.

sections.heading: Private placement meaning
sections.body: Offer to a select group other than by public offer, through private placement offer-cum-application.

sections.heading: Identified persons and cap
sections.body: Board-identified persons; number capped per financial year (excluding QIBs and s. 62 ESOP employees).

sections.heading: Offer form and no renunciation
sections.body: Prescribed offer and application to recorded persons; no right of renunciation.

sections.heading: Payment, allotment, refund
sections.body: Banking-channel payment; allot within 60 days or refund within 15 days thereafter with 12% interest.

sections.heading: Return of allotment
sections.body: Return of allotment must be filed as required.

examples.title: Compliant private placement
examples.body: Board identifies persons within the cap, issues prescribed offer forms without renunciation, receives banking-channel money, allots within 60 days and files return of allotment.

misconceptions.trap: Private placement has no numerical limit.
misconceptions.correction: Section 42 caps the number of identified persons per financial year (excluding QIBs and specified ESOP employees).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should Section 42 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify private placement vs public offer. II. Test identified persons and numerical cap. III. Check offer form, payment, 60-day allotment/refund. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Name the section and list ingredients.
State 60-day allotment and 12% interest on late refund.
